en.name: Hyacinth of Poland
en.summary: Polish Dominican missionary known as the "Apostle of the North" for spreading the faith across Poland, Ukraine, and the Baltic, credited with numerous reported miracles.
en.body: Hyacinth was a Polish nobleman-cleric who met Dominic in Rome and, deeply impressed, joined the recently founded Dominican order, returning to Poland to found the order's first house there before undertaking extensive missionary journeys across Poland, Lithuania, Ukraine, and reportedly as far as Kiev and the Black Sea region, earning him the title Apostle of the North. Numerous reported miracles accumulated around his missionary career in the centuries following his death, most famously an account that during the Mongol sack of Kiev he carried both the Blessed Sacrament and a heavy stone statue of the Virgin Mary to safety across a river, the statue reportedly becoming light enough to carry only after he prayed, and a separate tradition crediting him with walking across the surface of a river during a flood. He founded numerous monasteries across the region that anchored Catholic life there for centuries afterward. He died in 1257 and was canonized in 1594.
